items.title: Kering stock trades lower as Gucci's turnaround lifts H1 jewelry growth
items.summary: Kering shares eased 0.28% to EUR57.06 on August 13 despite Gucci's Q2 revenue decline narrowing to -2% (from -8% prior quarter) and a 0.4pt margin improvement, as investors weighed mixed group growth against jewelry's 14% H1 surge. Piece notes divergent US ADR pricing (one line at $315.81, another down 3.28% to $31.55), reflecting continued investor caution on the pace of the Gucci reset despite operational green shoots.

items.title: 64-year-old luxury giant closes at least 217 stores, plans more
items.summary: Kering closed 84 net stores in H1 2026 (total down to 1,635 from 1,719), including 20 store closures specifically in North America, as part of a 100-closure target for the full year. CFO commentary frames the cuts as deliberate rationalization of underperforming, low-density retail locations rather than distress, alongside a reported return to comparable-sales growth in Q2.

items.title: Kering Chief De Meo Targets Higher Profitability, Gucci Rebound (Capital Markets Day follow-up coverage)
items.summary: Continued analyst and press digestion of CEO Luca de Meo's three-phase Gucci turnaround plan (structural reset through 2026, rebuild through 2028, category leadership by 2030), with US wire coverage crediting stronger North America handbag demand -- notably new Borsetto and Paparazzo styles -- as the earliest tangible sign the reset is gaining traction with American consumers specifically.

items.title: "Gucci's quality issue" community thread
items.summary: Active PurseForum thread where US-based collectors compare notes on inconsistent Gucci leather-goods quality control -- citing plastic-feeling leather on some units and canvas panels that fail to line up -- with several posters noting the issue is factory-dependent rather than universal. Members report Gucci customer service resolves most complaints but describe the wait and inconsistency itself as eroding confidence in paying full retail.

items.title: Gucci Resale Value: Do Bags Hold Up? (2026 Guide)
items.summary: Resale-market analysis for US secondhand buyers/sellers notes current, popular Gucci styles typically resell at 55-80% of retail, but flags that older or dated styles can fall to 30-50%, and that some styles which retailed near $2,000 at peak are now trading for $600-900 on resale platforms -- a data point resale-focused shoppers cite as evidence of softening demand for non-hero Gucci pieces specifically.

items.title: TikTok haul/review content around the Gucci Vanity top-handle bag
items.summary: Sustained TikTok creator activity under #bagtok and Gucci-Vanity-tagged videos showing US shoppers unboxing and styling the Vanity medium top-handle bag in its three wearing configurations; comment threads mix positive styling praise with price-per-wear skepticism. Per-video metrics are not exposed via the public discovery aggregator, so volume is directionally strong but individual engagement figures are unavailable.

items.title: @gucci Instagram engagement holds at roughly average tier for luxury peers
items.summary: Third-party engagement audit of Gucci's official Instagram (50.6M followers) shows an engagement rate around 3.45%, averaging about 134K likes and 2K comments per post -- described by the auditor as merely average versus comparable luxury megabrand accounts, suggesting large campaign reach is not converting into outsized organic enthusiasm relative to peers like Chanel or Dior.

items.title: Gucci.com reviews continue to show recurring durability/repair complaints
items.summary: Ongoing pattern in Trustpilot reviews from US-heavy reviewer base: hardware chipping within months of purchase, fur-trim shedding without replacement offered, and a high-value handbag's faulty coating classified by Gucci as normal wear rather than a defect. Overall review sentiment is mixed rather than uniformly negative, but the durability/customer-service complaint thread recurs across independent reviewers day over day.
